Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will start with a new module today on corrosion chemistry.

Key details

  • Today's class we will understand what is corrosion, the different types of corrosion, the electrochemical theory of corrosion, and finally we will look at corrosion of iron.
  • Whenever the metal surface is exposed to the environment, the environment is going to cause this destruction of the metal.
  • It could be water or it could be simply moisture in the air, acids, bases, salts, oils, aggressive metal polishes and other types of solid and liquid chemicals.
  • And what is important for us to know is that it is a spontaneous process.
  • means whenever a metal is exposed to the environment, the reaction is going to be spontaneous.
  • We need not supply any energy for the process to take place.
  • And that is the reason why the moment the metal is exposed to any of these chemicals it is undergoing corrosion.
  • And most importantly, corrosion is a nuisance for us because it is not just the direct metal loss, it is the indirect losses which happen when corrosion takes place.
  • There could be oil pipelines which would get burst.
  • So all these are going to result in colossal losses, and therefore corrosion becomes very, very important study for us.
  • What exactly happens during corrosion?
  • We know that pure metal.
  • Is getting converted into undesirable products.
  • We made structures made of pure metal, but they are getting converted into undesirable products.
  • Rusting of iron is something all of us have experienced.
  • There is a reddish brown scale which is getting formed on the iron and steel objects.
  • And what is this?
  • This is actually hydrated ferric oxide.
  • And many times in the when you have these copper articles, we see that they get a greenish.
  • color on the surface.
  • It is due to basic pupric carbonate.
  • Another phenomenon which we obser observe and that is due to corrosion.
  • It is getting converted into CUCO3 plus C U O H twice.
